scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: validate a bearer token (async, may return null user ID), then load user preferences from DB (async, may not exist), then load their recommended items (async, may not exist). Short-circuit at the first absent value. No nested callbacks or intermediate awaits between chain steps.
criteria: Uses .bindAsync() to chain the async optional steps on Option (the chain may start from Option.from() or Option.fromAsync())
Does not await or call .then() between chain steps: each step is chained directly on the async Option (an await inside a step's callback is fine)
Returns OptionAsync, Promise<Option<T>>, or a Promise of a plain value produced by .match()/.orElse() at the end of the chain, not nested nulls

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: authenticate an API token (async, returns Either<ApiError, UserId>), fetch the user (async, returns Either<ApiError, User>), check admin role (sync). Return typed errors at each step. Show consumption with match at the end.
criteria: Uses .bindAsync() to chain async Either steps

Runs the sync admin check with .bind() directly on the async Either chain, in the same chain as the .bindAsync() steps (not wrapped in .bindAsync()/Promise.resolve and not after an intermediate await)
Uses .match() at consumption point to handle both success and error cases (awaiting chain.match(...) on the async chain, or .match() on the awaited Either)

scenarios.prompt: Express + Prisma + Redis pipeline: parse raw body (sync), validate schema (sync), check rate limit from Redis (async), save to Prisma (async), publish event to queue (async). Each step can fail. Stop on first failure and return structured error.
criteria: Uses sync .bind() for sync steps and .bindAsync() for async steps in the same chain
Does not await between chain steps — stays fluent
Error type propagates consistently through the entire chain

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: load a user's subscription with db.subscriptions.find(userId): Promise<Subscription | null>, ignore it if it has expired (subscription.expiresAt < new Date()), then load its plan with db.plans.find(subscription.planId): Promise<Plan | null>. Return the plan name, or 'free' when any step yields nothing. Keep it as one chain with no awaits between steps.
criteria: Uses .filter() directly on the async Option chain to drop an expired subscription (not an if inside a bindAsync callback or a separate await)
Chains the plan lookup with .bindAsync() on the same chain, without awaiting or calling .then() between steps
Ends the chain with .orElse('free'), .orElseAsync() or .match() to produce the plan name

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: call billingApi.getInvoice(id): Promise<Invoice>, which may reject with network or HTTP errors. Turn any failure into an ApiError { code: 'UPSTREAM'; message: string }, then reject unpaid invoices with { code: 'UNPAID' } (sync check), log a warning with the error code whenever the pipeline fails, and return EitherAsync<ApiError, Invoice>. No try/catch and no awaits between steps.
criteria: Wraps the call with TryAsync.runAsync() (or Try.runAsync()) and joins the Either pipeline with .toEither()
Maps the caught error to the ApiError with .mapLeft() and runs the unpaid check with .bind(), both directly on the async Either chain
Logs failures with .onLeft() on the async Either chain instead of awaiting and checking isLeft()
